title: Right Alt + Copilot (F23) shortcut causes stuck modifiers and unexpected keyboard behaviour on virtual desktops

comment.body:
Thanks for the exact shortcut, Windows/build details and the comparison between editors. Before changing modifier handling, please provide:
1. Only the relevant active mapping rows, or sanitized Keyboard Manager configuration with unrelated mappings and personal paths removed.
2. The keyboard language/layout and physical press/release order for Right Alt and Copilot. If possible on a test desktop, say whether it occurs with only the intended mapping enabled.

This distinguishes overlapping mappings or AltGr/compound-key state from an editor serialization problem.

information_gaps.why_needed: Determine whether overlapping source shortcuts are actually present and select the correct engine input
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Share only the relevant mapping rows or sanitized Keyboard Manager module configuration; remove unrelated mappings and personal paths.
information_gaps.information: The relevant active Keyboard Manager mappings as saved by the new editor

information_gaps.why_needed: Right Alt can imply AltGr/Left Control, and the Copilot key may emit a compound shortcut

initial_investigation: Read the report, all current comments, labels, assignees and linked-work timeline; checked for existing coverage before proposing work.
Traced shortcut event matching and modifier release/restore cases in KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp, including the Right-Alt/Left-Control state handling.
Checked existing modifier/Copilot handling and focused issue search. No existing linked fix or exact reproducing key-event sequence was established.
Reassessed the complete current issue discussion and timeline, including the latest maintainer labels. Label changes alone do not satisfy unanswered evidence requests or prove a repair.
inferences: A mismatch between physical Copilot/AltGr modifier state and synthetic release/restore handling is plausible; the editor or virtual desktops have not been isolated as the cause.
issue_context.summary: Right Alt/Copilot remapping can leave modifier-like behavior after closing an application on a virtual desktop.

plan: Load the actual sanitized mapping into the engine tests and model the physical press/release sequence, including AltGr if applicable.
Trace which source mapping wins, which synthetic modifiers are released, and which original modifiers are restored; correct only the demonstrated imbalance or duplicate serialization path.
Add regression rows for single/overlapping mappings, different key-up orders and closing the foreground application while preserving legitimately held modifiers.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a compound Copilot/Right-Alt source overlaps another mapping or restores a modifier after its physical release.

confidence.rationale: The symptom and engine state boundaries fit the hypothesis, but the active mapping, layout and key sequence are missing. No local reproduction or editor-regression claim is made.

proposed_fixes.title: Balance modifier state for the effective Copilot shortcut
verification: After the shortcut closes the application, typing F and Z is ordinary text and Win/virtual-desktop navigation remains normal; legitimate held modifiers still work.
